title: GOOD: pub use re-export instead of type shim for UserCredential
description:
## What

In crates/reader/src/config.rs line 7, the local UserCredential struct definition was replaced with:

    pub use stoa_auth::UserCredential;

This re-exports the canonical type directly into the reader config module's public namespace, so all 5 call sites (server_stores.rs, dispatch.rs, and 3 test files) that previously used `crate::config::UserCredential` continue to resolve without any import changes.

## Why good

The alternative was a type-conversion shim: keep the local struct but add `impl From<crate::config::UserCredential> for stoa_auth::UserCredential` and update every call to `CredentialStore::from_credentials` to convert the slice. That alternative adds runtime code, a From impl that must stay in sync if fields are ever added, and requires touching every call site.

The re-export is a zero-cost identity: it makes the reader module's `UserCredential` and stoa_auth's `UserCredential` the same type at the Rust type system level. No conversion, no divergence risk, zero call-site changes.

## Alternative avoided

A type alias (`type UserCredential = stoa_auth::UserCredential;`) would work nearly as well but is slightly worse: type aliases are not re-exports and do not participate in trait coherence in the same way; `pub use` is the idiomatic Rust idiom for re-exporting a type into a module's public API. The decision correctly uses `pub use`.
